solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Sees term transformed into something similar (8)

indicators.note: the letters of 'sees term' are changed into a new arrangement

annotation.surface: Someone watches a word morph into a close relative of itself.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the fodder: a semester is something similar to a term, the word the clue has just used, so 'term' does double duty in the reading.
annotation.definitionFit: A semester is a half-year academic period, much like a school term.

entries.clue: South American vessel or East Asian boat (6)

blocks.note: a pan is a cooking vessel

annotation.surface: A choice between a South American ship and an Asian boat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'South American' reads as one idea, a vessel from that continent; split it into S and AM, and 'vessel' becomes a kitchen pan rather than a ship.
annotation.definitionFit: A sampan is a small flat-bottomed boat used in China and South-East Asia.

entries.clue: Expert wrongly faults me over one of the three R’s (9)

indicators.note: 'faults me' set down wrongly means its letters in a different order
in a down clue, the R sits under the rest, so the rest is over it

blocks.note: the three R's are reading, writing and arithmetic; R stands for any of them

annotation.surface: A pupil complains that an expert has marked them down in one of the basic school subjects.
annotation.walkthrough: The R is part of the anagram fodder, not a fixed letter: jumble FAULTSME with R. 'The three R's' is a set phrase for the basics of schooling.
annotation.definitionFit: Masterful can mean highly skilled, as in a masterful performance.

entries.clue: Champion ahead in game (7)

indicators.note: 'ahead in game' says the ahead-word sits in the game-word, so UP is placed inside SPORT

blocks.note: up = ahead, as in 'two goals up'

annotation.surface: A champion is leading during a match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Champion' looks like a noun for the winner; it is the verb, to champion a cause, which is to support it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: to champion a cause is to back it and argue for it.

entries.clue: Sinister English upset Ireland (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns EIRE upside down, reading ERIE

blocks.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

annotation.surface: An ominous Englishman has offended Ireland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reads as a verb about causing offence; here it flips EIRE, and Lake Erie appears inside the answer as a bonus.
annotation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange in a frightening way, close to sinister.

entries.clue: Damage rascal with broadcast (6)

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child
to air a programme is to broadcast it

annotation.surface: A rogue damages things by what he puts out on the airwaves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks like an anagram indicator; it is the verb AIR.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to make something worse or weaker, as eyesight can be harmed.

entries.clue: Butterfly about in part of spring (7)

indicators.note: 'about in part of spring' puts the about-word within the month, so ON sits inside MARCH

blocks.note: on = about, as in a talk on birds

annotation.surface: A butterfly flutters about during springtime.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Part of spring' suggests a coil or a water source; it is a month of the season.
annotation.definitionFit: The monarch is a large orange-and-black migratory butterfly.

entries.clue: Greatest boxer briefly penetrated defence (5)

indicators.note: BIT is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: bit (as teeth penetrate) minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A famous boxer briefly broke through his opponent's guard.
annotation.walkthrough: The boxing picture makes 'defence' a guard in the ring; it is a legal defence, an account of being elsewhere.
annotation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence that the accused was somewhere else at the time.

entries.clue: State of ruler is good, in fact (8)

indicators.note: 'good, in fact' places the good-letter within the fact-word, so G sits inside REALITY

annotation.surface: A claim that a ruler's condition is sound in reality.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' reads as a nation governed by the ruler; it means condition, the condition of being royal.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the -ity suffix names a condition, and the condition of being regal is royal status or kingship.

entries.clue: Sturdily built son hiding in copse (8)

indicators.note: something hiding in a copse is surrounded by it, so S goes inside THICKET

blocks.note: a thicket is a dense clump of trees or bushes

annotation.surface: A burly boy is hiding in a small wood.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition and the container word are close cousins: 'thick' already suggests sturdy, so the solver half-sees the answer before the son is tucked in.
annotation.definitionFit: Thickset describes someone heavily and solidly built.

entries.clue: Perhaps I’m mistakenly reaching conclusion, failing to understand (15)

indicators.note: 'Perhaps I'm' arranged mistakenly gives its letters in a new order
the jumble reaches ENDING, which follows it

annotation.surface: Someone admits they may have jumped to the wrong conclusion and misunderstood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' looks like a hedge; it is fodder. 'Reaching conclusion' reads as coming to a judgement but simply puts ENDING after the jumble.
annotation.definitionFit: To misapprehend is to misunderstand, so misapprehending means failing to understand.

entries.clue: Plant people put back inside in top condition (7)

indicators.note: to put something back is to send it the other way, so MEN is written back to front
the reversed people are put inside the phrase for top condition

blocks.note: A1 = first-rate; the 'in' here is part of the phrase

annotation.surface: A gardener's instruction to replant flowers once they are healthy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a verb telling people to put something back; it is the noun. A1 (A ONE) is the standard crossword way to say first-class.
annotation.definitionFit: The anemone is a flowering plant of the buttercup family.

entries.clue: Warm and cold air mixed (7)

indicators.note: the letters of 'cold air' are mixed up

annotation.surface: A weather report of warm and cold air masses meeting.
annotation.walkthrough: The weather picture makes 'Warm' a temperature; it is warm as in friendly.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of friendliness: a cordial greeting or host shows heartfelt goodwill.

entries.clue: Frequently ring London newspapers (8)

blocks.note: the Financial Times, a London paper

annotation.surface: Someone keeps phoning the London press.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Newspapers' is plural because two London papers are wanted, the FT and The Times, the very paper this crossword appears in.
annotation.definitionFit: Ofttimes is an old word for often, frequently.

entries.clue: Inappropriately form altered emphasis (8)

indicators.note: the letters of 'emphasis' are altered into a new order

annotation.surface: An editor complains that a form was badly changed and its emphasis shifted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Form' looks like a noun, a document; it is the verb, to shape.
annotation.definitionFit: To misshape is to form something badly or wrongly.

entries.clue: Heroin to some extent creates addiction (5)

annotation.surface: A warning that heroin causes a certain amount of dependency.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To some extent' looks like a hidden-word signal; it is simply A BIT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the drug-use sense: a user 'has a habit' when dependent on a substance.

entries.clue: Balkan citizen welcoming to American citizen (9)

indicators.note: a host welcoming a guest takes them in, so BOSNIAN takes TO inside itself

blocks.note: a Bosnian is from Bosnia in the Balkans

annotation.surface: A person from the Balkans makes an American visitor welcome.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Welcoming to' reads as one phrase, but 'to' is the letters being welcomed. 'Citizen' appears twice on purpose: once in the wordplay, once in the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: people from Boston, Massachusetts, are one kind of American citizen.

entries.clue: Cultural object regularly written into key piece of information (8)

indicators.note: take every other letter of 'written'
'written into' is meant literally: the letters are written inside A FACT

blocks.note: a fact is a piece of information

annotation.surface: A museum object bears an important inscription.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key piece of information' reads as one phrase meaning vital fact; 'key' is split off to give the note A.
annotation.definitionFit: An artefact is a man-made object of cultural or historical interest.

entries.clue: US, for example, wanting inn as reminder of the past (5)

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the republic goes without its inn

blocks.note: a pub is an inn; it is removed

annotation.surface: A remark that America without its old taverns loses a link to history.
annotation.walkthrough: Removing PUB from the middle of REPUBLIC leaves RE and LIC, which close up.
annotation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from an earlier time.

entries.clue: Vehicle used when battling a disturbance after church (7)

blocks.note: a riot is a public disturbance

annotation.surface: A brawl breaks out after the church service.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase, 'Vehicle used when battling', and it borrows the surface's fighting: the battle looks like the disturbance, but it belongs to the chariot.
annotation.definitionFit: The chariot was a two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle used in ancient warfare.

entries.clue: I get up having rested first and take off (8)

indicators.note: 'having rested first' says the resting happened before the getting up, so SAT leads

annotation.surface: Someone describes getting up after a sit and setting off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take off' suggests leaving or an aircraft departing; it means to mimic or parody.
annotation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic them mockingly, which is to satirise them.

entries.clue: Man’s prosperous firm forming merger (7)

indicators.note: the two words merge, sharing the H where they meet

annotation.surface: A businessman's thriving company is being merged with another.
annotation.walkthrough: The business picture makes 'firm' a company; it is the adjective HARD. RICH ends and HARD begins with H, so merged they share one.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: 'man' in crosswords often stands for any male first name, and Richard is one.

entries.clue: Form of accommodation assimilating second to create another (6)

definitions.note: 'another' means another form of accommodation, leaning on the wordplay's opening words

indicators.note: to assimilate is to absorb into oneself, so HOTEL takes S inside

blocks.note: a hotel is one form of accommodation

annotation.surface: One kind of lodging absorbs a second and becomes a new one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Form of accommodation' looks like the definition, but it is the wordplay; the definition is the final word, 'another', meaning a second form of accommodation.
annotation.definitionFit: A hostel is cheap shared accommodation, often for travellers.

entries.clue: Rubbish in front of elm and two other trees (7)

indicators.note: take the first letter of 'elm'

annotation.surface: Litter lies before an elm and a couple of neighbouring trees.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish in front of elm' reads as litter lying there; 'in' is only a link.
annotation.definitionFit: Eyewash is nonsense, talk meant to deceive: rubbish.

entries.clue: What is more, it can be taken out of context randomly (5)

indicators.note: the answer is lifted out of the letters of 'context randomly'

annotation.surface: A complaint that a remark can be quoted out of context at random.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Randomly' looks like an anagram indicator, but it only supplies RA; the answer runs across the gap between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Extra, as an adverb, means additionally, which is what 'what is more' says.

entries.clue: Put in charge by clubs in game, player blows it (7)

indicators.note: 'put ... in game' is an instruction to place the letters, not a sporting selection
'in game' means within the game-word, so IC and C sit inside POLO

annotation.surface: A sports captain chosen by the clubs messes up the match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blows it' suggests a player ruining things; read literally, it is what a musician does to a piccolo.
annotation.definitionFit: A piccolo is a small flute, an instrument its player blows.

entries.clue: Run into parents in ham and cheese place (5)

indicators.note: 'run into parents' reads as meeting them, but here the run-letter goes inside the parents

blocks.note: R = run, as in cricket scoring

annotation.surface: Bumping into Mum and Dad at the deli.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ham and cheese place' sounds like a sandwich shop; it is the Italian city behind Parma ham and Parmesan.
annotation.definitionFit: Parma in Italy gives its name to Parma ham and Parmesan cheese.

entries.clue: It is parliament that’s reformed, including one opposed to colonies (4-11)

indicators.note: the letters are formed again in a new order
the I is included in the fodder

annotation.surface: A reformed parliament now includes someone against empire.
annotation.walkthrough: The political surface makes 'reformed' sound like constitutional change; it only rearranges letters, and 'one' adds the fourth I.
annotation.definitionFit: An anti-imperialist opposes empire-building and the holding of colonies.

entries.clue: Closed pen containing area that’s warm and cosy (6)

indicators.note: a pen holds animals in, and here the closed pen holds the area-letter

blocks.note: a door that is to is closed
a sty is a pig pen

annotation.surface: A shut enclosure with a snug space inside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool; it is the animal enclosure. TO for closed comes from 'pull the door to'.
annotation.definitionFit: Toasty means comfortably warm and snug.

entries.clue: Kind of sin or virtue — or expert on the difference? (8)

blocks.note: the seven deadly sins and the principal virtues share an adjective meaning chief
a senior Catholic churchman, presumed to know sin from virtue

annotation.surface: A question about who best knows right from wrong.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful, hence the question mark: a cardinal of the Church is presumed to be an authority on telling sin from virtue.
annotation.definitionFit: Cardinal describes both the seven deadly sins and the principal virtues, and names a prince of the Church.
